items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I joined Lionel Hampton’s band from Les Hite’s band. And I was in Lionel Hampton’s band in 1943 at the time I went into the service.

ctx.x: Did you get to do some traveling at that point, around the country, did you travel?

Yes, we traveled quite a bit, right. And from that band, I finally went, I joined Lionel Hampton’s band from Les Hite’s band. And I was in Lionel Hampton’s band in 1943 at the time I went into the service.
Can you give — we have a student sitting watching this tape — can you give him an idea of what it was like to be in a large group, and crisscrossing the country at that time?

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: When I left Les Hite I joined the Lionel Hampton band

ctx.x: You know I was so thrilled in a way and surprised too that I ended up for instance in Les Hite’s band because I was 19 years old and this was quite an experience for me, and I remember when I left Philadelphia on a bus to go to Lansing, Michigan to join Les Hite’s band and my mother accompanied me to the bus terminal, and I can remember my mother standing, as I had the window down and the bus is loaded with people, and my mother saying, “don’t you do anything to embarrass this family while you’re away.” And I…

rather surprised and I was actually in awe of most of the fellows who were in those bands. They were a little older than me. Some of them were in my age group but a lot of them were older and had a lot more experience. So I felt kind of lucky to be there. When I left Les Hite I joined the Lionel Hampton band, which at that time was roaring, and I was really in awe of that band. I mean I was again quite happy that I became a member. But it’s strange because the first trumpet player was Carl George and he was…
It wasn’t the easiest gig in the world, from what I understand.

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I must say at that time I admired Lionel, but I didn’t like the conditions that he created for the band.

ctx.x: Did you find you changed your own style to fit into the band?

I think I did. In fact, I know I did. I had to, because, when I went in, I was playing some of the lead parts the way I had been playing in Les Hite’s band, and Fred Beckett in particular would turn around and say, “What was that?” Literally made fun of it. Then I caught on to the style of their band, and it was a big help, but it took me a while to do it. I must say at that time I admired Lionel, but I didn’t like the conditions that he created for the band. The band was treated like we were shackles or…
How long did you stay with the band?
